title: BluePeak Analytics — first API onramp discovery
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-11-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Reynolds (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Terry Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Jordan Hale (BluePeak CTO), Samir Patel (BluePeak Lead Eng), Lena Ortiz (BluePeak Privacy)
summary: Intro / qualifying call for BluePeak's evaluation of Redwood's hosted API with discussion of quickstart path, free credits, time-to-first-token, and later Dedicated/Private considerations. Key concerns: data residency, SSO, latency SLAs for inference, and benching throughput vs cost. Agreed next steps: share security pack, provide $5k credits sandbox, schedule 1-hr performance pilot next week.
topics: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private fit for BluePeak use cases
Security & compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
Performance: latency SLOs, batching, KV cache and quantization
Credits, pricing model, and pilot logistics
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i see we have jordan, samir and lena from bluepeak. quick intro from our side — I'm Alex, AE on the PLG team, Maya is our solutions eng, Terry in CS to help with onboarding.
[00:18] Jordan (BluePeak CTO): hey team, thanks. we wanted to get a sense of how fast we can get an inference pipeline up using your hosted API and what the tradeoffs are if we move to dedicated later. cost is a big one.
[00:27] Maya (Redwood SE): great, yeah we'll cover quickstart which is usually minutes to first token for a simple generate call. typical path is self-serve signup, drop in API key, test with a small prompt set; we give sandbox credits so you can exercise the endpoints.
[00:45] Samir (Lead Eng): "minutes" sounds optimistic — what are we talking about in practice? latency per request? do you have cold-starts?
[00:55] Maya: yeah totally. for a standard text generation with one of our verified open models, first few requests may be a bit slower if nothing is cached, but within a session you hit sub-200ms for short prompts on hosted for the 8k sequence typical case; depends on model size, truncation, streaming vs non-streaming.
[01:18] Jordan: sub-200ms — that's good. Our SLAs for product features want 200-300ms p95. Also, we can't send PII offsite for some customer segments — that's why we're evaluating private later.
[01:30] Lena (Privacy): can you summarize your data residency and retention defaults for hosted? we have strict retention rules.
[01:38] Alex: absolutely. hosted by default keeps logs for 30 days unless you opt-in to longer storage; there's a private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) for regulated datasets. we also integrate with customer KMS for key separation for Redwood Private. I'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs after.
[01:52] Samir: ok. on the perf side — Maya, can you explain how batching affects latency vs cost, and how you do kv cache? sometimes these vendor docs gloss over the cache details.
[02:05] Maya: sure. we have continuous batching in the runtime — it groups tokens across concurrent requests but we also have smart routing so latency-sensitive calls can pin to low-batch fast lanes. KV cache is per-session to reuse past context; some transcriptions of the tech call call it K-V cash, ha — but it's basically key/value cache for attention states so you avoid recomputing prefixes. That reduces effective token compute — helpful for chat histories.
[02:32] Jordan: if we start on hosted, can we measure cost-per-response and then move to Dedicated if we need guaranteed throughput? what's the on-ramp look like?
[02:40] Terry (CSM): customers often start with free credits and our self-serve console, do 1-2 week sandbox and then if you need committed throughput we do Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools. Migration is API-compatible, you can pin model versions so it should be low-friction.
[02:55] Samir: what about private? we'd need VPC peering and our own KMS. any air-gapped options?
[03:02] Alex: yes, Private supports VPC and there's an on-prem package for very strict environments. For KMS we can integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSMs depending on your setup.
[03:12] Jordan: cool. can you give an example timeline — from signup to a small pilot with, say 10k requests?
[03:20] Maya: sure. self-serve sign up -> API key -> run quickstart samples same day. If you want to run a perf pilot we give credits and setup a dedicated sandbox region; usually 3-5 business days to run representative bench tests and iterate on prompts. Private/on-prem takes longer, 4-8 weeks typically.
[03:38] Jordan: that aligns. Samir: what telemetry do we get? token-level cost breakdown?
[03:45] Terry: yes console gives token breakdown, per-route latency, tracing hooks and per-request metadata. You can ingest logs to your SIEM.
[03:55] Lena: SSO is mandatory for us, and we need RBAC — can Redwood integrate with our SAML provider?
[04:02] Alex: yep SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC roles in console. We'll include the integration guide in the security pack.
[04:12] Jordan: competitors — are there major differences vs the usual cloud endpoints like vendorA and vendorB?
[04:18] Maya: in short, we're focused on production economics — batching, KV cache, prioritized fast lanes. Competitors often have simple endpoints but less tuning for high-throughput inference or require more ops. i'd say vendorA is similar on model catalog but less on cost controls; vendorB is more managed but higher unit cost.
[04:38] Samir: we've heard about quantized models — do you support 4-bit or 8-bit quantization for production inference?
[04:44] Maya: yes, we have quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize; for serving we support int8 and experimental int4 paths with validated quality/latency tradeoffs. we'll share sample evals.
[04:55] Jordan: let's talk quickstart: what do you give in credits and what's the real limit?
[05:01] Terry: we typically offer a $5k sandbox credit for pilot evaluation for teams this size with an add-on to extend. It covers token spend and embedding calls. For PLG we also give a small free credit on sign-up to explore.
[05:12] Jordan: good — that helps. Samir: network egress — if we use hosted, are there options to route through our VPC for egress control?
[05:20] Alex: hosted is in Redwood-managed infra, but for egress controls you can use Private with VPC peering. We also have dedicated tenancy with some network controls.
[05:30] (brief crosstalk)
[05:40] Maya: one thing to flag — the fastest time-to-first-token is usually for basic REST generate; streaming helps perceived latency for UI. For benchmark scripts we recommend a mixture of streaming and non-streaming to reflect real UX.
[05:58] Samir: can you run a small A/B on model variants? e.g., cheaper quantized vs baseline to see regen quality delta?
[06:06] Maya: yes, rollouts and A/B tests are supported in console — we can stage traffic and automatically fallback if quality metrics degrade.
[06:14] Jordan: ok. any typical gotchas?
[06:18] Alex: prompt design always — token usage can spike with verbose prompts. Also attention to streaming vs full response costs. For large context we recommend prefix caching.
[06:30] Lena: legal question — do you sign data processing addendum (DPA) and can we get contractual residency clauses?
[06:37] Alex: yes DPA is standard and we can discuss contractual residency for enterprise deals, that's usually part of Private/reserved contracts.
[06:45] Jordan: sample bench — how would we test latency?
[06:48] Maya: we provide a benchmark harness (link in notes) but quick approach: pick 1000 representative prompts, run with concurrency levels and measure p50/p95/p99. We'll also show how batching and fast lanes change those numbers.
[07:03] Samir: could we run that next Wednesday?
[07:06] Alex: should be doable — we'll provision credits and a sandbox tenant.
[07:10] Jordan: what about cost predictability — we don't want surprise spikes from bursty usage.
[07:15] Terry: you can set budget alerts, rate limits and quotas; Dedicated gives predictable unit economics via reserved capacity. For hosted we provide burst protection and automatic fallbacks to cheaper variants when needed.
[07:27] Samir: is the API spec standard OpenAI-like?
[07:30] Maya: it's REST and RPC-friendly, similar shapes for generate and embeddings, but we also support function calling and structured outputs. We include SDKs in Node/Python and sample apps.
[07:40] Jordan: any reference customers in fintech? we have compliance needs and want to see similar setups.
[07:47] Alex: yes — we'll include a short reference list; some are in payments and some in healthcare.
[07:54] (pause)
[08:02] Lena: small nit: audit logs need to include token-level hashes not raw text — can you support that?
[08:08] Maya: yes we can redact or hash request data in logs and support field-level redaction in Private.
[08:15] Jordan: okay good. let's talk timeline + next steps.
[08:18] Alex: recapping: BluePeak will try hosted quickstart using sandbox credits; we'll provide security pack + SOC2; Maya will help design a bench plan and run pilot next Wednesday. Also we'll show a migration plan to Dedicated and Private.
[08:33] Jordan: agreed. Samir: one last technical — how do you do model failover if a particular GPU pool is degraded?
[08:40] Maya: smart routing — automated fallback to compatible model variants in other pools/regions; can pin to dedicated pool if you need absolute isolation.
[08:48] Jordan: that covers most. thanks everyone.
[08:51] Alex: cool. we'll follow up with the security pack and the credits details.
[09:00] (meeting moves to quick questions then ends)

Note: timestamps above are front-loaded; rest of meeting included deeper back-and-forth in the bench plan (~minutes 09–30), a prompt engineering demo snippet (~30–40), and pricing/practical admin (~40–47). Some transcribed words may be imperfect (e.g., vendor names, 'K-V cash').
